subject: Marginal posterior for the total over a projection grid

messages.author: 72c025ccfc1fb009
messages.subject: Marginal posterior for the total over a projection grid
parts:
Hi there, 

probably a simple answer for this. I am using the SPDE functionality in INLA. I have a simple model like below

y~poisson(mu)
mu = exp(Beta0 + Au)

where u are random effects with a matern co variance, and A projects from vertices to observation space. I also have a projection matrix P which projects the latent field over the spatial domain of interest. I can project the

prediction = exp(Beta0 + Pu)

Can I get marginal distribution for sum(prediction)?

Thanks in advancements.

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Marginal posterior for the total over a projection grid
parts:
On Mon, 2019-11-25 at 19:53 -0800, Cyril Marsh wrote:
> prediction = exp(Beta0 + Pu)
>
> Can I get marginal distribution for sum(prediction)?

essentially, only by simulation. you can use

inla.posterior.sample

and then

inla.posterior.sample.eval

to evaluate \sum exp(\linearPredictor_i)

you may need to weight the sum taking into account the areas of the mesh, etc.

see the 'LGCP' paper by Dan Simpson et al, in Biometrika a few years ago
